sources.title: A connectome of the male Drosophila central nervous system
claims_used: Canonical identities and row order for 815 motor neurons.
Motor body-family labels ad, am, fl, hl, hm, ml, nm, pm, rm, wm and xm.
Peripheral sensory class, subclass, entry nerve and side annotations.
The paper reports 805 motor neurons assigned to broad body categories and distinguishes neck, retina, antenna, proboscis, ingestion and digestion families.
sources.implementation_effect: Defines all motor and nonvisual afferent rows. Broad family labels permit body-part masks but do not establish muscle-to-servo direction.

sources.title: Organization of circuits linking descending input to motor output in the Drosophila Male Adult Nerve Cord connectome
claims_used: Supplement 3 publishes MN body IDs, types, systematic types, exit nerves, targets, match certainty and literature/line evidence.
T1 leg identities were matched to FANC and light microscopy; 198 T1 identities were transferred to T2/T3 by serial homology.
Wing anatomy includes steering, DLM/DVM power, pleurosternal, tergopleural and TTM families; haltere anatomy includes one power and seven steering muscles.
Many abdominal and neck targets remain unresolved.
sources.implementation_effect: Supports 156 side-resolved diagnostic cohorts covering 400 MaleCNS rows. These labels remain inter-animal inferred and never become arbitrary joint directions.

sources.title: A complete connectome of the Drosophila ventral nerve cord
claims_used: FANC is the female VNC reference used by MANC authors for cross-animal motor-neuron matching.
sources.implementation_effect: Makes the fine target layer an inter-animal inference rather than a direct MaleCNS measurement.

sources.title: Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain-neck-body connection
claims_used: MANC/FANC homolog tables are cross-animal identity evidence, not measured neuromuscular mechanics.
sources.implementation_effect: Prevents homolog labels from being promoted to measured muscle-to-axis mappings.

sources.title: Connectome-constrained networks predict neural activity across the fly leg proprioceptive system
claims_used: Femoral chordotonal claw neurons encode joint position, hook neurons encode movement direction, and club neurons respond to vibration.
sources.implementation_effect: Keeps joint position and velocity ports modality-aware. Individual FANC neuron identities are not copied onto MaleCNS rows.

sources.title: FlyGym and NeuroMechFly v2
claims_used: Micro-CT-derived articulated fly morphology with 69 author body segments and 126 biological joint axes in yaw-pitch-roll order.
Author low-level active walking subset contains 42 leg axes; the model supplies position servos and synthetic adhesion rather than anatomical muscles.
sources.implementation_effect: Defines exact joint and M90 actuator identity/order. The selected nonleg servos, gains and adhesion controls remain engineered.

sources.title: FlyMimic
claims_used: The released muscle/tendon model provides anatomical actuators for the left front leg only; examples drive other legs with direct torques.
sources.implementation_effect: Useful anatomical evidence for a future front-leg muscle layer, but insufficient to invent a whole-body MaleCNS muscle atlas.
